reference: Bash type/help builtin contracts and util-linux column for runnable parity. Parity cases run the same deterministic script on both shells with private relative fixture files; expected behavior is not derived from bash-os output.
coverage: Bash metadata: column is registered as a builtin and help -s advertises its documented synopsis.
util-linux table output with default whitespace separators, ragged rows, explicit field separators, empty fields, and a custom output separator.
util-linux non-table layout with explicit output width, column-first versus row-first filling, and explicit space padding.
Named relative file operands, an unterminated final input record, repeated redirected stdin in one shell, and invalid output-width handling.
Nonempty zero-width list and table modes, ragged explicitly separated tails, repeated dash operands, and a custom identity banner.
G66: display-width -t padding under UTF-8, -N/--table-columns, -n/--table-name and -J/--json.
Guest pass 5 G81: -R/--table-right, -l/--table-columns-limit, -H/--table-hide and -O/--table-order with util-linux 2.41 column lists (names, numbers, ranges, 0, -1, '-'), and no header without data.

Guest pass 6 G96: -d/--table-noheadings, -L/--keep-empty-lines, -e/--table-header-repeat (LINES page height), -r/--tree with -i/-p (ASCII, UTF-8 and JSON), and -T/-W/-E against an explicit -c width on single-row tables.
Pass 8 (G120): option errors in GNU form, naming the command only, with the GNU status.
exclusions: Only the column command is covered; the sibling col and colrm builtins are outside this suite.
Terminal-derived default width, wide-character display alignment, and util-linux options outside the implemented column subset are not covered.
No privileged, host-system, hardware, or network operation is part of column's selected behavior, so no operation case is deferred.
A column named twice in -O is placed once; util-linux 2.41 then also drops another column, which is not reproduced.

How util-linux 2.41 splits a too-narrow -c width among several -T/-W/-E columns over multi-row tables is reproduced only approximately (libsmartcols' distribution is not documented), so only single-row width cases are compared.

cases.purpose: Use Bash's type -t contract to confirm that the statically registered column command is recognized as a builtin with an empty candidate PATH.
cases.script: type -t column

cases.purpose: Check that Bash help exposes the registered column synopsis and includes its documented table and row-fill options.
cases.script:
synopsis=$(help -s column)
if [[ $synopsis == *column* && $synopsis == *-x* && $synopsis == *-t* ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'column synopsis advertised'
else
  printf '%s\n' 'column synopsis missing' >&2
  exit 1
fi

cases.purpose: Compare table mode's default whitespace splitting and column alignment across mixed spaces, tabs, leading whitespace, and a shorter final row.
cases.script:
printf '  NAME	AGE  CITY  
Al 8 NY
Beatrice	12	Los Angeles
Cy 4
' > rows.txt
column -t < rows.txt

cases.purpose: Compare colon-separated table parsing, preservation of empty fields between adjacent separators, and a multi-byte output separator.
cases.script:
printf 'name::id:path\nx:long:7:/\n' > rows.txt
column -t -s ':' -o ' | ' < rows.txt

cases.purpose: Compare non-table vertical filling at an explicit width with deterministic short items and a final incomplete row.
cases.script:
printf 'red
blue
green
black
white
' | column -c 18

cases.purpose: Compare -x row-first item ordering against the same explicit-width non-table fixture.
cases.script:
printf 'red
blue
green
black
white
' | column -x -c 18

cases.purpose: Compare the implemented --use-spaces padding mode at a fixed output width instead of tab-separated columns.
cases.script:
printf 'oak
pine
ash
elm
' | column --use-spaces=2 -c 17

cases.purpose: Compare table input from two private relative file operands, including a final record without a newline.
cases.script:
printf 'key value\nshort 1' > first.txt
printf 'longer 22\n' > second.txt
column -t first.txt second.txt

cases.purpose: Run column repeatedly in one shell with fresh redirections to the same relative file; each invocation must independently process all rows.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > repeated.txt
for pass in 1 2 3; do column -t < repeated.txt; done

cases.purpose: Zero width is accepted with empty stdin; the separate nonempty case determines its formatting behavior.
cases.script: column -c 0

cases.purpose: Exercise zero width with nonempty list and table input; raw formatting is compared.
cases.script:
printf 'one\ntwo\nthree\n' > items
column -c 0 items
column -x --output-width=0 items
column -t --output-width 0 items

cases.purpose: Missing cells must retain padding and separators through the final table column.
cases.script:
printf 'a:b:c:d
long:z
x::
' | column -ts: -o ' | '

cases.purpose: Keep the existing bash-loadable identity banner as a custom contract, separate from external version output.
cases.script: column --version

cases.purpose: Repeated dash operands share stdin once per invocation; each fresh redirection reads the complete stream. Expected bytes follow the documented logical-stream extension.
cases.script:
printf 'A' > input
column -t - - < input
column -t - - < input

cases.purpose: Whitespace-only records are ignored (column manual); actual ragged records retain their missing-cell padding. Compare default and explicit separators plus list mode without trimming output.
cases.script:
printf 'a:b:c

   
long:z
:
' > input
column -ts: input
printf 'a b c

	
long z
' | column -t
printf 'one

   
two
' | column -c 0

cases.purpose: Empty input is empty; negative output width is rejected diagnostically.
cases.script: : > empty; column -t empty; column -c -1 empty

cases.purpose: Ordinary negative widths fail with util-linux status 1 across short, attached and both long spellings, even for empty input; a later zero-width invocation remains valid.
cases.script:
: > empty
for form in split attached long-split long-equals; do
 rc=0
 case $form in
  split) column -c -1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  attached) column -c-1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  long-split) column --output-width -1 empty || rc=$? ;;
  long-equals) column --output-width=-1 empty || rc=$? ;;
 esac
 printf 'negative-status=%s\n' "$rc"
 [[ $rc == 1 ]]
done
printf 'one\n' > data
column -c 0 data

cases.purpose: G66: under a UTF-8 locale -t pads by display width (wcwidth), so accented and double-width text aligns.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'é x
日本 y
z w
' > u
column -t u
column -t -o '|' u
printf 'a	b
日本語	c
' | column -t -s "$(printf '	')"

cases.purpose: G66: -N/--table-columns prints a header row in -t mode, with fewer or more names than fields.
cases.script:
printf 'a 1\nbb 22\nccc\n' > t
column -t -N NAME,VAL t
column -t -N X,Y,Z t
column --table --table-columns=K t
column -t -N 'Long Name',V -o ' | ' t

cases.purpose: G66: -J/--json with -N prints util-linux's JSON (lower-cased keys, null for missing cells, escaped strings, -n table name).
cases.script:
printf 'a 1\nbb\n' > t
printf 'q"x b\\y\n' > e
column -J -N Name,Val t
column --json --table-columns Name,Val --table-name Things t
column -J -N k,v e
column -J -s , -N a,b t
: > empty; column -J -N a empty; echo end

cases.purpose: G66: -J without -N, -N or -n without -t/-J, and a row wider than the names under -J fail with status 1.
cases.script:
printf 'a b c\n' > t
for args in '-J' '-N a,b' '-n x' '-J -N a,b'; do rc=0; column $args t || rc=$?; echo "$args rc=$rc"; done

cases.purpose: G81: -R/--table-right right-aligns columns named by number, -N name, range (A-B, clipped), 0 (all) or -1 (last not hidden); a right-aligned column is padded on the left, an empty last cell is not padded.
cases.script:
printf 'a 1 x\nccc 22 yyy\n' > T
printf 'a 1 x\nccc\n' > S
printf 'a 1\nccc 2\n' | column -t -R1
for r in 2 0 -1 1-2 3 3-1 2-9 ,1 1, '' 1,1; do echo "[$r]"; column -t -R "$r" T; done
column -t -N A,B,C -R B T
column -t -N A,B -R 3 T
column -t -N A,B,C,D -R D T
column -t -R 2 S
column -t -R 2 -R 1 T
column -t --table-right=1 T
column -t --table-right 3 T
column -tR1 T
printf 'aa b\nc dd\n' | column -t -R 1,2 -o '|'
column -t -N A -R - T

cases.purpose: G81: -l/--table-columns-limit N makes the N-th field the rest of the line: after a run of whitespace by default, after one separator with -s, trailing blanks kept; the last -l wins.
cases.script:
echo 'a b c' | column -t -l2
echo 'a   b   c   d' | column -t -l2
echo '  a   b   c   d  ' | column -t -l2
echo 'a:b::c:d' | column -t -s: -l2
echo 'a:b::c:d' | column -t -s: -l3
printf 'a b c\nd e\n' | column -t -l1
printf 'a\tb  c\n' | column -t -l 2
printf 'a  b  c\n' | column -t -l2 -s ' '
printf 'a b c d\ne f\n' | column -t -l 3 -N A,B
printf 'a b c\n' | column -t -l2 -N A,B -J
printf 'a 1 xx\nccc 22 yyy\n' | column -t -l 2 -l 3
printf 'a b\n' | column -t -l ' 2'
printf 'a b\n' | column -t --table-columns-limit=1
printf 'a b\n' | column -l 2

cases.purpose: G81: -H/--table-hide leaves out columns by number, name, range, 0, -1 or '-' (every unnamed column); the last visible column is then the unpadded one.
cases.script:
printf 'a b c
c d e
' > U
printf 'a b
c d
' | column -t -N X,Y -H Y
printf 'a b
c d
' | column -t -N X,Y -H X
for h in 2 0 -1 1-2 2,3 1; do echo "[$h]"; column -t -H "$h" U; done
column -t -N X -H - U
printf 'a b
' | column -t -H 1 -o :
printf 'a b c
' | column -t -H 1 -R 2 -o :
printf 'a b c
' | column -t -N A,B,C,D -H C
printf 'a b
' | column -t --table-hide=1
column -t -H 1 -H 2 U
printf 'a 1 xx
ccc 22 yyy
' | column -t -H 3 -R -1
printf 'a b c
' | column -t -N A,B,C -J -H B
printf 'a b c
' | column -t -N A,B,C -J -H A,B,C

cases.purpose: G81: -O/--table-order prints the named columns first, in that order, then the rest in input order; -H applies after it and -R -1 still names the last input column not hidden.
cases.script:
printf 'a b c\nd e f\n' > U
printf 'a 1 xx\nccc 22 yyy\n' > T
printf 'a b\nc d\n' | column -t -N X,Y -O Y,X
for o in 3 3,1 1,2 2,3 1,3 2,1 3,2 -1 -1,1 1,-1 01; do echo "[$o]"; column -t -O "$o" U; done
column -t -O 3 -H 2 U
column -t -O 3,1 -R 1 T
column -t -O 3,1 -R -1 T
column -t -O 3 -O 2 T
printf 'a b c\n' | column -t -O 2 -H 2 -o :
printf 'a 1 x\nccc\n' | column -t -O 2 -N A,B,C
printf 'a b c\n' | column -t -N A,B,C -J -O C
column -t --table-right=1 --table-hide 2 --table-order=3 --table-columns-limit=3 T

cases.purpose: G81: an unknown column name or number, -O 0 or a range in -O, a bad -l value, an option without its argument, and -R/-H/-O without -t exit 1.
cases.script:
printf 'a 1 x\nccc 22 yyy\n' > T
for args in '-t -R 4' '-t -R X' '-t -R 2-' '-t -R x-1' '-t -R +1' '-t -N a,B,c -R A' '-t -O 0' '-t -O 2-3' '-t -O 5' '-t -l 0' '-t -l x' '-t -l -1' '-t -l 2x' '-t -l 99999999999' '-R1' '-H1' '-O1' '-t -H'; do rc=0; column $args T > out || rc=$?; echo "$args rc=$rc $(wc -c < out)"; done

cases.purpose: util-linux prints no -N header when there is no data row, and then does not check -R names either.
cases.script:
printf '' | column -t -N A,B || echo rc=$?
printf '\n\n' | column -t -N A,B || echo rc=$?
printf '' | column -t -N A,B -R 5 || echo rc=$?
printf '' | column -t -R 5 || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: G96: -d/--table-noheadings prints the table without the -N header, while -N still names the columns for -R and -J.
cases.script:
printf 'a b c\nd e f\n' > T
column -t -N A,B,C -d T
column -t -N A,B,C --table-noheadings -R C T
column -t -d T

cases.purpose: G96: -L/--keep-empty-lines keeps blank and whitespace-only input lines as empty table rows and as empty fill-mode items; a table whose only lines are blank prints nothing and fails.
cases.script:
printf 'a b

c d
  
e f
' | column -t -L
printf 'a b

c d
' | column -L -c 30
printf 'a b

c d
' | column -L -x -c 30
printf 'a,b
  

c,d
' | column -t -s, -L
printf 'a b

c d
' | column -t -N X,Y --table-empty-lines -R 2
printf 'a b

c d
' | column -J -N x,y --keep-empty-lines
printf '

' | column -t -L || echo rc=$?
printf '

' | column -L || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: G96: -e/--table-header-repeat prints the header again at the top of every terminal page, the page height coming from LINES when output is not a terminal; -d turns the header (and the repeat) off.
cases.script:
seq 1 30 | sed 's/.*/& x/' > T
LINES=10 column -t -N A,B -e T
LINES=1 column -t -N A,B --table-header-repeat T | head -6
LINES=10 column -t -N A,B -e -d T | head -3
LINES=10 column -t -e T | head -3

cases.purpose: G96: -r/--tree with -i/--tree-id and -p/--tree-parent nests each row under the row whose ID matches its parent, in input order, with ASCII branch prefixes in the C locale; rows with an unknown parent stay at the top level and a later duplicate ID takes the children over.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C
printf '1 0 root
2 1 kid
3 1 kid2
4 2 grand
7 4 gg
8 4 gg2
9 3 k2c
5 0 other
6 5 x
10 99 orphan
' > T
column -t -r 3 -i 1 -p 2 T
printf '1 0 root
2 1 kid
3 1 kid2
4 2 grand
' | column -t -N ID,P,NAME --tree NAME --tree-id ID --tree-parent P -H ID,P
printf '4 1 late
1 0 root
' | column -t -r 3 -i 1 -p 2
printf '1 0 root
1 0 dup
2 1 kid
' | column -t -r 3 -i 1 -p 2
printf '1 2 a
2 1 b
3 3 c
4 0 d
' | column -t -r 3 -i 1 -p 2
printf '1 0 root
2 1 kid
3 1 kid2
4 2 grand
' | column -r 3 -i 1 -p 2

cases.purpose: G96: in a UTF-8 locale the tree uses box-drawing prefixes; with -J the tree is nested as "children" arrays instead of prefixes.
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf '1 0 root
2 1 kid
3 1 kid2
4 2 grand
5 0 r2
' > T
column -t -N ID,P,NAME -r NAME -i ID -p P T
column -J -N id,p,name -r name -i id -p p T

cases.purpose: G96: -r needs both -i and -p, the tree columns must exist, and every --table-* or tree option needs -t; each failure exits 1 with no output.
cases.script:
printf '1 0 root\n2 1 kid\n' > T
for a in '-t -N ID,P,NAME -r NAME -i ID' '-t -N ID,P,NAME -r NAME -p P' '-t -N ID,P,NAME -r NOPE -i ID -p P' '-t -r 7 -i 1 -p 2' '-T 1' '-E 1' '-W 1' '-d' '-e' '-i 1' '-p 1' '-t -T' '-t -T NOPE'; do rc=0; column $a T > out || rc=$?; echo "$a rc=$rc $(wc -c < out)"; done

cases.purpose: G96: with an explicit -c/--output-width, -T/--table-truncate cuts, -W/--table-wrap wraps and -E/--table-noextreme lets the named columns overflow, the other columns keeping their width; 0 or 'unlimited' disables the limit. Single-row tables, whose space split util-linux distributes deterministically.
cases.script:
L=$(printf '%040d' 0)
printf "$L $L 1\n" > T
column -t -T 1,2 -c 30 -N LONGHEADERNAME,BB,C T
column -t -T 1,2 -c 10 -N LONGHEADERNAME,BB,C T
column -t -T 1,2 -c 0 T
column -t -T 1,2 --output-width=unlimited T
printf 'aaa bbb ccc ddd,x\n' | column -t -s, -W 1 -c 12
printf 'aaa bbb ccc ddd,x\n' | column -t -s, --table-truncate 1 -c 12
M=$(printf '%060d' 0)
printf "a $M 1\n" | column -t -T 1,2 -R 2 -c 40
printf "a $M 1\n" | column -t --table-wrap 2 -c 40
printf "a $M 1\n" | column -t --table-noextreme 2 -c 40
printf "a $M 1\n" | column -t -T 2 -J -N a,b,c -c 40

cases.purpose: G120: an unknown long option is reported as column reports it, with no internal builtin name and the GNU status.
cases.script:
rc=0
column --bogus </dev/null || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"

cases.purpose: G120: an unknown short option is reported as column reports it, with no internal builtin name and the GNU status.
cases.script:
rc=0
column -Y </dev/null || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"

cases.purpose: G120: --table-columns without its argument.
cases.script:
rc=0
column --table-columns || rc=$?
echo "rc=$rc"
